tagline: Up the South Fork of the Payette, against the whitewater.
intro: At Banks the Banks-Lowman Road leaves Idaho 55 and heads east up the South Fork of the Payette River, through Garden Valley and Crouch, to meet Idaho 21 at Lowman. Going east it climbs nearly a thousand feet, with the river's whitewater coming down against it.
The road ties together two other byways, the Payette River at Banks and the Ponderosa Pine at Lowman, and in between it keeps to a river known for whitewater rafting and fishing.

moments.title: Banks
moments.text: The North and South forks of the Payette meet here, where the Staircase run on the South Fork ends and the Main run starts down toward Horseshoe Bend.

moments.title: Crouch
moments.text: Founded in 1934, the town incorporated in 1951 for a plain reason, to bring legal alcohol and gambling to the area.

moments.title: Lowman
moments.text: Hot springs surface in the middle of town, and the school is a one-room school, one of only a couple hundred still in use in the United States.
